company.name: Bombas
company.one_liner: Premium athletic socks: for every pair sold, a pair goes to a homeless shelter.

facts.summary: Two founders rebuilt the sock from scratch (cushioned footbed, arch support, seamless toe) and donate a pair for every pair sold, because socks are the most requested item at shelters.
highlights: Socks are the most requested clothing item at homeless shelters; Bombas donates a pair per pair sold.
Engineered for comfort: honeycomb arch support, cushioned footbed, seamless toe.
Sold direct-to-consumer online at a premium price.
The company is young; the Sharks questioned whether a sock company is worth $4M.

real_deal.summary: Daymond John invested $200,000 for 17.5% (about a $1.14M valuation).

outcome.headline: Over $1 billion in lifetime sales; often called Shark Tank's most successful company.
outcome.story: Bombas became a mission-driven apparel brand with over $1B in lifetime revenue and well over 100 million items donated. It's private, so the value here (~$1B) is an estimate based on reported revenue of roughly $300M a year.
